hidden_reference.target_name: L1 (isolated as L1.EA and L1.MeOH solvates)

source_documents.title: Solvent-dependent crystal forms of an o-phenylenediamine-derived Schiff base: ESIPT behaviour, photophysical properties and luminescent metal-ion sensing

reference_evidence_units.quote: Both compounds exhibit excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT), which dominates their fluorescence behaviour.
reference_evidence_units.subject: L1 (both solvate forms)
reference_evidence_units.statement: ESIPT is stated as the dominant emission mechanism.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Abstract claim; the emission data show a single band at 428-446 nm and no separately assigned keto band.

reference_evidence_units.quote: is attributed to the electronic transition of the intramolecularly hydrogen-bonded enol form, which is capable of undergoing excited-state intramolecular proton transfer
reference_evidence_units.subject: L1
reference_evidence_units.statement: A 360-370 nm absorption band is assigned to the H-bonded enol form able to undergo ESIPT.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Assignment of an absorption band, not a measurement of proton transfer.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Single-crystal X-ray diffraction revealed that both forms adopt the keto-amine tautomer in the solid state
reference_evidence_units.subject: L1.EA, L1.MeOH
reference_evidence_units.statement: The transferable proton sits on N in the crystal (keto-amine).
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Ground-state tautomer; says nothing about excited-state transfer.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Conversion of the KK tautomer into the KE tautomer requires overcoming a proton-transfer barrier of 2.26 kcal
reference_evidence_units.subject: L1
reference_evidence_units.statement: Low ground-state proton-transfer barriers between tautomers.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Ground-state calculation; no excited-state proton-transfer profile for the free ligand.

reference_evidence_units.quote: suggesting that aggregation and intermolecular interactions in the solid phase promote non-radiative deactivation of the excited states, thereby quenching the fluorescence of both compounds
reference_evidence_units.subject: L1.EA, L1.MeOH
reference_evidence_units.statement: Weaker solid-state emission attributed to aggregation-promoted nonradiative decay.

reference_mechanisms.label: ESIPT_PT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: ESIPT is the paper's stated mechanism; the support is indirect (enol absorption band, keto-amine crystal tautomer, ground-state barriers), with no keto emission or excited-state calculation for the free ligand.
